Jane — thanks for the heads up. We're able to provide a compact runbook and the sample logs. Quick clarifications so we send exactly what you need:

- 'Evacuate/evict a KEK' in our context is the emergency removal of a tenant wrapping key (KEK) from a node/pool when we detect suspected compromise or a failed HSM binding. Normal rotations are scheduled; this is the emergency path.
- Our emergency path uses an HSM-backed unwrap when available; if the tenant HSM is unavailable we execute a documented software-wrap fallback with split-keystore escrow and multi-signer authorization.
- We retain a signed audit voucher (operator ID + approval token) for every emergency eviction and ship the voucher to the immutable audit store.

I'll attach: a 2-page operator runbook (oncall_kek_evacuate_runbook_v1.pdf), a redacted operator shift log (operator-shift-log-sample.txt), and a CSV index of artifacts (soc2-witness-index.csv). Ben, Irene — looping you in to confirm the wording around escrow/signed vouchers and to confirm the drive link access.

Will deliver attachments in a follow-up email with the Drive/Docusign links and the indexed artifact list.

Best,

Thanks Tessa — confirmed. A few technical points to keep for the auditor narrative (Irene please chime in if I miss anything):

1) Authorization: Emergency KEK eviction requires a 2-of-3 operator approval (on-call lead + on-call SRE + Compliance manager) OR a documented incident commander sign-off if during Major Incident. The runbook shows the approval UI and the approval token format.

2) HSM vs fallback: When the customer-provided (BYOK) HSM is reachable we perform an HSM Unwrap using the tenant KEK-wrapping key; unwrap operation is recorded in the HSM audit log and a signed operator voucher is produced. If the HSM is unreachable, we use the split-keystore fallback (N-of-M quorum of operator HSM keys held by Redwood) and record the escrow reveal operation in the sealed audit file.

3) Evidence retention: Signed vouchers + HSM audit extracts are immutably archived for 7 years (Soc 2 requirement for this customer). We also include a checksum manifest in the witness CSV.

Irene — can you confirm the path to extract a 24-hour HSM access log and the redaction plan for tenant identifiers? I will also prepare the minimal playbook snippet we can share during the walkthrough.

-Ben
Ben Carter
